`paleytable` adds a Paley table, bringing the current catalog from 981 to 982 kinds (983 gallery choices including plain). 61×61 rounded-square tiles; tile (row, col) is the Legendre symbol of `col − row` modulo the prime 61 (the Paley construction): a difference of 0 (the diagonal) takes the middle tone, a nonzero square modulo 61 (a quadratic residue; there are 30 of them) takes bright rose pink and a non-residue takes dark plum; because 61 ≡ 1 (mod 4) the symbol is symmetric, and since the table depends only on `col − row` the whole table shows parallel diagonal bands and repeats seamlessly on the torus. The seed only moves the whole table around the torus, and only `(sx − sy) mod 61` of that shift makes a difference. It is a schematic number-theory pattern, not a real material.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 61×61 grid, the residue / non-residue / zero tones `0.14 + 0.7` / `0.14 + 0.1` / `0.14 + 0.4`, the rose and plum tones and the 0.3 m nominal tile are authored choices. The relief reuses the 0.0008 of the existing table kinds without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0378). I first expected exactly one matching torus shift per seed; the probe showed 61 (the table depends only on `col − row`), so the test now asserts that structure: the `sx − sy` of all 61 shifts is the same, and the `(sx − sy) mod 61` of the four seeds all differ. In the 512² preview each cell is about 8 pixels and the pattern shows as diagonal bands; I did not check cells one by one by eye.

It follows the table-tile sampler (the same shape as `hadamardmatrix`): at build time the nonzero quadratic residues of 61 are found by brute-force squaring (30 of them) and every cell's tone follows `(col − row) mod 61` (0 → 0.4, residue → 0.7, non-residue → 0.1, a Float64 table); every cell owns one compact-support rounded-square kernel (a quartic superellipse through smoothstep with a half width of 0.46 cell, exactly zero before the cell boundary, C1), color is `0.04 + (0.14 + tone − 0.04)·mask + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)`; height is `0.8·dome·(0.88 + 0.12·tone) + 0.08·grain`; gap AO is 0.6; roughness is a constant 0.4; metallic is 0; the cache totals 61² + 128² = 20,105 Float64 values / 160,840 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM; the residue set exists only during construction). Defaults are a 0.3 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). Measured (tool-run) at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7: on a 256² grid the lit area (color>0.5) covers 36.34%–36.42%, color is 0.0252–0.0259 to 0.8541–0.8545 with a mean of 0.4012–0.4014, the lowest AO is 0.6 and height is at most 0.8478–0.8486 relief; on a 512² grid the lit area covers 36.35%–36.36%, color is 0.0251–0.0254 to 0.8547–0.8549 with a mean of 0.4011–0.4014, roughness is a constant 0.4, the lowest AO is 0.6 and height is at most 0.8494–0.8504 relief; the colours at the 3,721 tile centres match the table written independently in the test at exactly 61 torus shifts (all with the same `sx − sy`, which is 51, 59, 10 and 23 modulo 61 for the four seeds; maximum error about 0.0148–0.0149, roughly the amplitude of the fine grain); the light masks (512²) of seeds 0 and 1 differ on 37.5% of pixels; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (116.7, 83.5, 99.1), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0378 and the minimum z component is 253. The test also checks the cell counts of the three tones (61 zeros, 1,830 residues and 1,830 non-residues). No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('paleytable', { size: 512, seed: 7, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`.

`hadamardmatrix` adds a Hadamard matrix, bringing the current catalog from 980 to 981 kinds (982 gallery choices including plain). 64×64 rounded-square tiles; tile (row, col) is entry (row, col) of the Sylvester Hadamard matrix: +1 (bright cool white) when the number of 1 bits in the bitwise AND of `row` and `col` is even and −1 (dark blue-grey) when it is odd; row 0 and column 0 are all +1 and every other row has equally many +1 and −1 entries (2,016 of the 4,096 entries are −1), and the whole is built from nested 2×2 blocks. The seed only moves the whole table around the torus. It is a schematic mathematical-matrix pattern, not a real material.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 64×64 grid, the +1/−1 tones `0.14 + 0.7` / `0.14 + 0.1`, the cool white and dark blue tones and the 0.3 m nominal tile are authored choices. The relief reuses the 0.0008 of the existing table kinds without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0378). The test's 256² grid has only 4 samples per cell and none of them lands on a gap centre, so on 256² the darkest color is 0.0927–0.0936 and the lowest AO 0.7344, unlike the 0.0251–0.0253 and 0.6 of the 512² grid; I first copied the "lowest AO equals 1 − gapOcclusion" assertion from other table kinds, then replaced it with the 256² range and added a sample at the corner shared by four tiles (1/64, 1/64) to confirm the AO is exactly 0.6 there.

I viewed the preview (seed 7): cool-white and dark blue-grey rounded tiles forming a fine pattern with a diagonal-stripe look; I could not make out the nested 2×2 block structure by eye (the correctness of every tile is confirmed by the test comparison above, not by looking). `levycurve` adds a Lévy curve, bringing the current catalog from 979 to 980 kinds (981 gallery choices including plain). A thin mint-green line on a dark teal-black ground traces the order-9 Lévy C curve: 512 unit steps in which step `k` heads in direction `i^popcount(k)` (`popcount` is the number of 1 bits in `k`; the directions cycle east, north, west, south), with 416 distinct lattice points and 462 distinct edges — 50 steps retrace an edge already walked, so some segments are drawn twice; its bounding box is about 39×39 cells on a 48×48-cell torus, so there is empty space around it and it does not join neighbouring tiles; the line is a third of a cell wide with a faint glow outside it. The seed only shifts the whole curve around the torus. It is a schematic fractal trace and the curve is not closed. It shares the trace sampler branch of `dragoncurve` and `peanocurve`; only the vertex list differs.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the order 9, the 48×48-cell torus, the one-third-cell line width, the tanh sharpness of 8, the mint and dark teal tones and the 0.25 m nominal tile are authored choices. The relief reuses dragoncurve's 0.0008 without further tuning (the maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps is 0.0543). I first checked the direction rule with a small independent script for the vertex and edge counts (order 9: 416 distinct points, 462 distinct edges, bounding box x −7 to 31, y −15 to 23) and then chose the torus size and offsets.

Defaults are a 0.25 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). Measured (tool-run) at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7 on a 256² grid: the lit area (color>0.5) covers 7.08%–7.12%, color is 0.0457–0.0459 to 0.8328–0.8339 with a mean of 0.1109–0.1112, roughness is 0.2001–0.3999, AO is always 1 and height is at most 0.9872–0.9944 relief; each seed's 144×144 node map equals the Lévy curve the test writes independently with bit counting at exactly one torus shift ((26, 39), (12, 40), (40, 7) and (29, 40); 1,340 lit nodes each); the node maps of seeds 0 and 1 differ on 11.3%; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (16.8, 46.0, 43.5), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0543 and the minimum z component is 252. `tulle` adds tulle, bringing the current catalog from 978 to 979 kinds (980 gallery choices including plain). A hexagonal honeycomb net knitted from fine ivory threads on a dark purple-black ground: pointy-top hexagons of circumradius 1, 7 columns × 8 rows (56 hexagons, 168 segments with each shared edge stored once) filling the tile; each thread is a compact-support quartic profile and the knots where three threads meet are brighter because the profiles add up. To let the honeycomb tile the square torus evenly, the horizontal and vertical periods are in the ratio `7√3 : 12`, which stretches the hexagons by about 1.04% (they are not regular). The seed only shifts the whole net around the torus (in steps of 1/64 of the tile). It is a schematic net textile, not a photograph of real tulle, and it is not translucent (the dark ground is just the colour behind the mesh).

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 7 columns × 4 row pairs, the thread radius of 0.15, gain 1.8, the ivory and dark purple tones and the 0.3 m nominal tile are authored choices. Tuning record: the first version used a thread radius of 0.2 and gain 1.5, the threads looked too thick in the preview, and I adopted 0.15 and 1.8 (I only looked at those two previews); at relief 0.0015 the maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps was 0.0643, and lowering it to 0.0012 gave 0.0424 (minimum z component 251 → 252). The first version of the probe's independent model had a bug (a wrong key in the edge de-duplication produced 176 segments instead of 168) and for seed 0xffffffff it found no matching shift; after fixing the de-duplication all four seeds had matching shifts.

A dedicated sampler: at build time, on a pointy-top honeycomb (width `√3`, row spacing 1.5), every hexagon contributes its east, north-east and north-west edges (each stored as a midpoint and a half-length vector, 168 of them, in four Float64 arrays); every sample converts its coordinates to honeycomb units (horizontal period `7√3`, vertical period 12), takes the point-to-segment distance to the nearest torus image of every segment, sums the weights `(1 − d²/r²)²` (r = 0.15, value and slope zero at the boundary, C1) and squashes the sum by `1 − exp(−1.8·sum)`; color is `0.08 + 0.78·thread + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)`; height is `0.85·thread + 0.15·grain`; roughness drops by 0.1 on threads (base 0.65); AO is always 1; metallic is 0; the cache totals 168×4 + 128² = 17,056 Float64 values / 136,448 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Defaults are a 0.3 m nominal tile and 0.0012 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). Every sample walks the 168 segments (skipping those out of reach); I did not measure the time, so no performance number is claimed. Measured (tool-run) at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7: on a 256² grid the lit area (color>0.5) covers 19.57%–19.59%, color is 0.0651–0.0657 to 0.8686–0.8695 with a mean of 0.2215–0.2217, roughness is 0.5505–0.65, AO is always 1 and height is at most 0.9827–0.9866 relief (on a 512² grid the lit area covers 19.65%–19.66%); each seed matches the independently rewritten honeycomb model of the test at 48 sample points for exactly 8 of the 64 × 64 candidate torus shifts (maximum error 0.0113–0.0138, roughly the amplitude of the fine grain), and these 8 shifts are the honeycomb's own translation symmetry (x mod 32 and y mod 8 fixed); the light masks (512²) of seeds 0 and 1 differ on 33.8% of pixels; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (74.7, 69.8, 74.3), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0424 and the minimum z component is 252. `sacksspiral` adds a Sacks spiral, bringing the current catalog from 977 to 978 kinds (979 gallery choices including plain). On a dark navy-black ground the integers 1 to 500 are laid out as dots on a Sacks spiral: the integer `n` sits on an Archimedean spiral at radius `0.45·√(n/500)` (in tile units) and angle `2π√n`, so the perfect squares line up along one ray; primes (95 of them) are bright gold dots and composites are dim gold-brown dots, with the primes particularly dense along a few curved arms. The spiral is centred in the tile and does not reach the tile edge, so tiles do not overlap; on the torus every tile holds one disc-shaped spiral. The seed only turns the whole spiral by a whole number of degrees (0 to 359). It is a schematic number-theory pattern, not a star chart or a photograph.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 500 integers, the radius of 0.45, the dot radius of 0.014, the gold and navy tones and the 0.4 m nominal tile are authored choices. Tuning record: the first version (dot radius 0.012, prime tone 0.7, composite tone 0.2, gain 2, relief 0.0008) had dots that looked small and dim in the preview, and the probe measured a brightest value of 0.667, a mean of 0.077 and a maximum normal tilt² of only 0.0048 in the 512² maps; after changing to a dot radius of 0.014, prime tone 0.85, composite tone 0.3, gain 3 and relief 0.002 the brightest value is 0.871, the mean 0.111 and the maximum tilt² 0.0441, and the rotation fit (exactly one whole degree per seed) was the same for both versions.

A dedicated sampler: at build time trial division decides whether each `n = 1 … 500` is prime, and the position of every integer is stored in two Float64 arrays (plus a Uint8 prime flag); every integer owns one compact-support quartic dot (weight `(1 − d²/r²)²` with radius 0.014, value and slope both zero at the boundary, C1); primes and composites are summed separately and squashed into [0, 1) by `1 − exp(−3·sum)`; color is `0.05 + 0.85·prime dots + 0.3·composite dots·(1 − prime dots) + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)`; height is `0.6·prime dots + 0.25·composite dots·(1 − prime dots) + 0.1·grain`; roughness drops by 0.15 on primes (base 0.4); AO is always 1; metallic is 0; the cache totals 500×2 + 128² = 17,384 Float64 values (139,072 B) plus a 500 B prime flag array, all lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Every sample walks the 500 integers (skipping those beyond the radius); I did not measure how long this takes at 512², so no performance number is claimed. Defaults are a 0.4 m nominal tile and 0.002 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). Measured (tool-run) at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7: on a 256² grid the lit area (color>0.5) covers 2.93%–2.96%, color is 0.0355–0.0358 to 0.8670–0.8696 with a mean of 0.1114–0.1115, roughness is 0.2575–0.4, AO is always 1 and height is at most 0.6547–0.6647 relief (on a 512² grid the lit area covers 2.94%–2.95%); at exactly one whole-degree rotation per seed (298°, 161°, 4° and 107°) the colours at the centres of all 500 dots match the independently rewritten model in the test (maximum error 0.0143–0.0148, roughly the amplitude of the fine grain); in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (33.7, 32.8, 37.1), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0441 and the minimum z component is 252. `peanocurve` adds a Peano curve, bringing the current catalog from 976 to 977 kinds (978 gallery choices including plain). `divisorcount` adds a divisor-count table, bringing the current catalog from 975 to 976 kinds (977 gallery choices including plain). 48×48 rounded-square tiles; cell (col, row) stands for the integer `n = row × 48 + col + 1` (1 to 2304) and is toned by the number of divisors `d(n)`: primes (`d = 2`, 342 of them) are dim, composite numbers with many divisors (highly composite numbers) glow, and the largest `d` in the table is 40 (at `n = 1680`); because each row has 48 cells, a multiple of 12, the columns holding multiples of 12 form conspicuous bright vertical bars, with fainter bars for multiples of 6, 4 and so on. The seed only moves the whole table around the torus, so the statistics stay the same and only the position changes. It is a schematic number-theory table, not a mineral or a photographed material.

`dragoncurve` adds a dragon curve, bringing the current catalog from 974 to 975 kinds (976 gallery choices including plain). A thin golden line on a dark purple-black ground traces the order-9 Heighway dragon curve: 512 unit steps whose turns follow the regular paper-folding sequence (step `k = 2^m(2j+1)` turns left for even j and right for odd j); the curve touches itself at lattice points but never shares an edge (361 distinct lattice points, 512 edges); its bounding box is about 27×32 cells on a 40×40-cell torus, so there is empty space around it and it does not join neighbouring tiles; the line is a third of a cell wide with a faint glow outside it. The seed only shifts the whole curve around the torus. It is a schematic fractal trace, not folded paper, and it is not closed.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the order 9, the 40×40-cell torus, the one-third-cell line width, the tanh sharpness of 8, the gold and dark purple tones and the 0.25 m nominal tile are authored choices. Tuning record: the first version had a half-cell line width (2 lattice nodes per cell), and neighbouring lines almost merged into a block in the preview, so I changed it to 3 nodes per cell (a third-cell line width); while changing the width I updated only the connector coordinates and missed the cell-point coordinates, which left large regions of isolated dots in the preview, and the probe counted 1,376 lit nodes against 1,385 expected; after fixing the cell-point coordinates the count was 1,385. At relief 0.0015 the maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps was 0.1602 and the minimum normal z component was 244; lowering it to 0.0008 gave 0.0517 and 252 (before and after values from the same probe).

A dedicated sampler: at build time the 512 steps are walked from the paper-folding sequence; on a 120×120 lattice the cell points sit at every third coordinate (361 of them) and the two connector nodes between consecutive cells fill the gap (1,024 of them), for 1,385 lit nodes in total; the curve coordinates get a fixed offset of (9, 10) plus the seed's torus shift; `latticeField` blends them with the C1 smoothstep and re-sharpens with `0.5 + 0.5·tanh(8·(pattern − 0.5))`; color is `0.06 + 0.76·line + 0.1·glow·(1 − line) + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` where `glow` is the unsharpened blend times `(1 − 0.14·9×9 noise)`; height is `0.8·line + 0.2·grain`; roughness drops by 0.2 on the line (base 0.4); metallic is 0; the cache totals 120² + 9² + 128² = 30,865 Float64 values / 246,920 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Defaults are a 0.25 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). Measured (tool-run) at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7 on a 256² grid: the lit area (color>0.5) covers 9.38%–9.44%, color is 0.0457–0.0460 to 0.8329–0.8337 with a mean of 0.1359–0.1361, roughness is 0.2001–0.3999, AO is always 1 and height is at most 0.9871–0.9940 relief; each seed's 120×120 node map equals the independently rewritten dragon curve of the test at exactly one torus shift ((11, 27), (38, 16), (6, 16) and (13, 25); 1,385 lit nodes each); the node maps of seeds 0 and 1 differ on 16.0%; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (48.5, 34.3, 37.8) and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0517. I viewed the preview (seed 7): a golden gridded dragon line on dark purple, repeated over the torus. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('dragoncurve', { size: 512, seed: 7, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`.

`juliatiles` adds Julia tiles, bringing the current catalog from 973 to 974 kinds (975 gallery choices including plain). A mosaic of a Julia set (`c = −0.8 + 0.156i`) made of 64×64 rounded-square tiles: cell (col, row) takes the complex number at its centre (real and imaginary parts both from −1.6 to 1.6) as `z₀` and iterates `z → z² + c`, and its tone is the escape iteration count (`|z| > 2`, at most 64) over 64 under a square root, from dark red-brown (fast escape) to bright orange (many iterations before escaping, near the set boundary); cells that never escape (404 of them, about 9.9%) are the darkest brown-black. The tiles are raised and the gaps darker with occlusion (AO), and the seed only moves the whole table around the torus. With only 64×64 resolution it is a pixel-art Julia set; it shares the sampler branch of `mandelbrottiles` and differs only in the start point and the constant.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 64×64 grid, the window of −1.6 to 1.6, the constant c = −0.8 + 0.156i, the 64-iteration cap, the square-root tone mapping, the red-brown and orange tones and the 0.3 m nominal tile are authored choices. The first preview was adopted, and the relief of 0.0008 reuses the result tuned for mandelbrottiles without further adjustment.

It reuses the `mandelbrottiles` sampler branch (which now serves `juliatiles` too): in Julia mode `z₀` is the complex number at the cell centre and `c` is the fixed constant −0.8 + 0.156i, iterating `z → z² + c` until `|z|² > 4` or 64 iterations; the tone table (Float64) holds `√(iterations/64)` and cells that never escape are recorded as −1 (colour 0.02); every cell owns one compact-support rounded-square kernel (a quartic superellipse through smoothstep with a half width of 0.47 cell, exactly zero before the cell boundary, C1); color is `0.04 + (level − 0.04)·mask + 0.02·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` with `level = 0.1 + 0.82·tone` (0.02 inside the set); height is `0.8·dome·(0.88 + 0.12·tone)` (0.5 times that inside the set) plus `0.08·grain`; gap AO is 0.7; roughness is a constant 0.4; metallic is 0; the cache totals 64² Float64 values (the tone table) + a 128² fine grain = 20,480 Float64 values / 163,840 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Defaults are a 0.3 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). Measured (tool-run) at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7 on a 512² grid: the light area (color>0.5) covers 6.48%–6.51%, color is 0.0102–0.0104 to 0.9212–0.9227 with a mean of 0.2152, roughness is a constant 0.4, the lowest AO is 0.7 and height is at most 0.8724–0.8746 relief; the colours at the 4,096 tile centres match the Julia escape times rewritten independently in the test (404 cells never escape), with exactly one torus shift per seed ((1, 5), (2, 59), (55, 24) and (22, 21) for the four seeds) and a maximum error of 0.0100 (the amplitude of the fine grain); the light masks of seeds 0 and 1 differ on 11.7% of pixels; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (73.7, 39.7, 35.2) and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0421. I viewed the preview (seed 7): a Julia set on a red-brown ground with bright orange dots and fractal dendrites along its boundary, cut at the picture edge by the seed's torus shift. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('juliatiles', { size: 512, seed: 7, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`.

`mandelbrottiles` adds Mandelbrot tiles, bringing the current catalog from 972 to 973 kinds (974 gallery choices including plain). A mosaic of the Mandelbrot set made of 64×64 rounded-square tiles: cell (col, row) iterates `z → z² + c` at the centre `c` of its small patch of the complex plane (real part from −2.2 to 0.8, imaginary part from −1.5 to 1.5), and its tone is the escape iteration count (`|z| > 2`, at most 48) over 48 under a square root, from dark blue (fast escape) to bright cyan-blue (many iterations before escaping, near the set boundary); cells that never escape (726 of them, about 17.7%) are the darkest blue-black. The tiles are raised and the gaps darker with occlusion (AO), and the seed only moves the whole table around the torus. With only 64×64 resolution it is a pixel-art Mandelbrot set, and the set is not continuous across the torus seam, so it is not a seamless fractal.

At relief 0.0012 the maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps was 0.0865; lowering it to 0.0008 gave 0.0399 (before and after values from the same probe).

`rhodoneatable` adds a rose-curve table, bringing the current catalog from 971 to 972 kinds (973 gallery choices including plain). A pink-neon table of rhodonea curves: 6×6 cells, where cell (col, row) draws `r = cos(k·θ)` with `k = (col + 1)/(row + 1)` (θ from 0 to 2π·(row + 1), so every rational k closes), from single circles through three- and four-petal roses and many-petal flowers to tangled rings, with a faint glow on a dark purple-black ground; the seed only rotates all the roses by one angle (0 to 0.5 radians). It is a mathematical pattern and not a real neon tube (no tube width variation, end electrodes or reflections). The diagonal cells with k = 1 are a small circle through the cell centre.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or neon photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 6×6 grid, the amplitude of 0.4 cell, the 192-point polyline, the line width of 0.018 cell, the pink and purple-black tones and the 0.3 m nominal tile are authored choices. The line treatment reuses the version just tuned for `lissajoustable` (`lineGain = 4` and a compact glow kernel), so it did not go through the beading and cell-boundary jump problems again; the first preview was adopted and the relief of 0.0008 was not adjusted.

A dedicated sampler: at build time each cell's rose `r = 0.4·cos((col + 1)/(row + 1)·θ)` is taken as a closed 192-point polyline at `θ = 2π·(row + 1)·k/192` (in cell units relative to the cell centre, all rotated by a seed-chosen angle); every sample computes the squared distance to each of the cell's 192 segments, the line is `1 − exp(−4·Σ exp(−d²/0.018²))` (a Gaussian sum, so no crease where the rose crosses itself) and the glow is `1 − exp(−0.1·Σ smoothstep(clamp(1 − d²/0.1²)))` (a radius of 0.1 cell, which does not exceed the shortest distance of 0.1 cell between the rose and the cell boundary, so it is zero there); color is `0.04 + 0.74·line + 0.12·glow·(1 − line) + 0.02·(128² fine grain − 0.5)`; height is `0.8·line + 0.2·grain`; roughness drops by 0.2 on the line; the cache totals 2×6×6×192 = 13,824 Float64 values (the polyline points) + a 128² fine grain = 30,208 Float64 values / 241,664 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Defaults are a 0.3 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). Cost: every sample measures the 192 segments of its cell; on this machine under bun a 512² sampling took about 232–243 ms and 512² maps about 257 ms (single measurements, not a benchmark). Measured (tool-run) at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7 on a 512² grid: the lit area (color>0.5) covers 25.48%–25.53%, color is 0.0301 to 0.7896–0.7899 with a mean of 0.2483–0.2484, roughness is 0.2–0.4 and height is at most 0.9961–0.9988 relief; the maximum color at the four corners of each cell is 0.0489–0.0493; scanning 101 rotation angles between 0 and 0.5 radian, exactly 29–30 angles put all 6×6×64 = 2,304 rose points on pixels brighter than 0.5 (minimum 0.7598–0.7617) while the other angles do not; the lit masks of seeds 0 and 1 differ on 15.0% of pixels; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (72.3, 40.3, 66.2) and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0469. I viewed the preview: pink roses on a dark purple ground, instantly a rhodonea table, with the cells of larger k dense like woven discs. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('rhodoneatable', { size: 512, seed: 7, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`.

`lissajoustable` adds a Lissajous table, bringing the current catalog from 970 to 971 kinds (972 gallery choices including plain). An oscilloscope-style green phosphor table of curves: 6×6 cells, where cell (col, row) draws the Lissajous curve `x = sin((col + 1)·t + φ)`, `y = sin((row + 1)·t)` (frequency ratio (col + 1):(row + 1), from ellipses to tight weaves) with a faint glow on a dark green-black ground; the seed only changes the common phase φ (0.25π to 0.75π). It is a mathematical pattern and not a real oscilloscope screen (no graticule, scan lines or noise).

`primesieve` adds the sieve of Eratosthenes, bringing the current catalog from 969 to 970 kinds (971 gallery choices including plain). A 32×32 grid of rounded-square tiles standing for the integers 1 to 1024: primes (172 of them) are bright gold, 1 is dim, and a composite is toned `0.4·(1 − 1/p)` by its smallest prime factor `p` (multiples of 2 are darkest and composites with larger factors slightly brighter), so the multiples of 2, 3, 5 and 7 leave regular vertical bars and diagonals on an olive ground with the primes scattered among them. The tiles are raised and the gaps darker with occlusion (AO), and the seed only moves the whole table around the torus. It is a number-theory pattern, not any real material; the contrast between composites is low, so it reads as gold dots on an olive ground.

`collatzsteps` adds Collatz stopping times, bringing the current catalog from 967 to 968 kinds (969 gallery choices including plain). A 32×32 grid of rounded-square tiles where cell (col, row) stands for the integer `n = row·32 + col + 1` (1 to 1024) and its tone is the number of Collatz steps (halve an even n, triple an odd n and add 1) needed to reach 1 divided by 178 (the longest below 1025 is 178 steps for n = 871), varying continuously from dark purple to warm orange. The tiles are raised and the gaps darker with occlusion (AO), and the seed only moves the whole table around the torus. It looks like structured noise (neighbouring integers have subtly related step counts, but the whole is close to random); it is not any real material, only a mathematical pattern.

`modulartable` adds a modular multiplication table, bringing the current catalog from 965 to 966 kinds (967 gallery choices including plain). A mosaic of 31×31 rounded-square tiles where the tone of cell (col, row) comes from the mod-11 multiplication-table residue `((a + col)·(b + row)) mod 11` (11 steps from dark purple to golden yellow, with the seed choosing the offsets a and b), the tiles raised and the gaps darker with occlusion (AO). Because a residue of 0 occurs whenever `a + col` or `b + row` is a multiple of 11, whole rows and columns turn into bands of dark tiles, and the rest shows the symmetric multiplication-table pattern. It is not any real mosaic or tiling, only a mathematical pattern.

`elementaryautomata` adds elementary cellular automata, bringing the current catalog from 964 to 965 kinds (966 gallery choices including plain). Four Wolfram elementary automata side by side on an amber LED matrix (each band 32 rows by 128 columns with the columns joined on a ring): rule 30 (the chaotic triangle from a single live cell), rule 90 (the Sierpinski triangle), rule 110 (a complex asymmetric structure) and rule 184 (diagonal traffic-flow stripes from a repeating "110" start pattern); the seed only rotates the columns of the whole picture and the pattern itself is fixed. Each cell is a rounded-square LED and unlit LEDs stay dark brown. Because the columns form a ring, the triangles of rules 30, 90 and 110 do not reach the edge within 128 columns, so they look the same as on an infinitely wide row.

`hilbertcurve` adds a Hilbert curve, bringing the current catalog from 962 to 963 kinds (964 gallery choices including plain). One cyan circuit trace on a dark navy ground follows an order-4 Hilbert space-filling curve: each of the 16×16 cells is visited exactly once, and the end is joined to the start across the tile seam to close the loop (the start and end of a Hilbert curve are neighbouring cells on a torus); the line is about half a cell wide with a faint glow outside it. The seed picks one of the eight square symmetries (mirror and transpose) and shifts the curve around the torus, so the statistics stay the same and only the orientation and position change. It is not a real circuit board (no pads, vias or multiple layers).

`quasicrystal` adds a quasicrystal-style interference pattern, bringing the current catalog from 961 to 962 kinds (963 gallery choices including plain). Five plane waves with integer wave vectors at nearly 72° steps interfere into a blue-and-white pattern that looks five-fold symmetric: dark blue dots, pentagon rings and star-like shapes over a pale blue ground. Because every wave vector is an integer, the pattern is **exactly periodic over the tile**, so it is an approximation by five-wave interference and not a true quasicrystal or Penrose tiling (the vector lengths are 14 and about 13.6 and the angles are 0°, 72.9°, 144.0°, 216.0° and 287.1°, only approximating equal 72° steps); the seed changes only the wave phases and the statistics stay the same.

`spectrogram` adds spectrogram, bringing the current catalog from 947 to 948 kinds (949 gallery choices including plain). A spectrogram-style surface on a deep blue ground: 12 horizontal yellow harmonic lines bent into waves by vibrato, 5 vertical broadband burst bands and scattered speckle, with a time-frequency energy field deciding where it shows (patches fade). It is not a real audio spectrum, real harmonic ratios, time/frequency scales, a colour-scale legend or text; every harmonic has the same vibrato depth (real higher harmonics wobble more), and colour is a single linear dark-blue-to-bright-yellow gradient rather than the multi-colour scales common on real spectrograms.

This material is an authored schematic of the general look of a spectrogram. No specific source document, photograph, audio data or measurement is cited and no real spectrogram was compared; the harmonic count (12), vibrato depth and cycles, drift amount, energy-field resolution and threshold, burst count and weight, the deep blue and bright yellow tones, roughness and the 0.3 m nominal tile are authored choices.

A dedicated sampler draws the harmonic lines as an integer number (12) of `exp(−sin²(π·12·(v − shift))/w²)` (C-infinity, wrapping with the tile) with shift = `(0.2·sin(2π·6·u) + 0.18·(drift(u) − 0.5))/12` (vibrato plus a slow drift from an 8×2 periodic noise field); the bursts are an integer number (5) of vertical `exp(−sin²(π·5·u)/w²)`; the speckle is a 96×96 periodic noise field; all three are multiplied by a smooth gate from a 20×14 energy field, `0.5 + 0.5·tanh(5·(noise − 0.35))`, and joined by the union `1 − Π(1 − x)` so intensity stays in [0, 1]; the cache totals 16 + 280 + 9,216 + 16,384 = 25,896 Float64 values / 207,168 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Colour is pigment mapped from intensity (0.04 + 0.9 × intensity), height is about 0.6 relief × intensity plus 0.4 relief of paper grain; roughness is always 0.4; metallic is 0, there is no mortar and AO is 1. Defaults are a 0.3 m nominal tile and 0.002 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). Measured (tool-run) at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 512² grid: bright lines (color>0.5) cover 6.31–6.76%, color is 0.0400–0.939 with a mean of 0.155–0.161 and height is at most 0.971–0.982 relief; the harmonic line position follows the vibrato (about +0.2 of a spacing at a positive vibrato peak and about −0.2 at a negative one, verified by the tests for each seed, with a tolerance including the drift's upper bound of 0.09); the bright-area masks (color>0.2) of seeds 0 and 1 differ on more than 5% of pixels; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (50, 41, 67), r>128 covers 7.0% and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.092. I viewed the preview: neat yellow wavy lines and vertical bright bands on a deep blue ground that read as a stylised spectrogram, but too regular (all harmonics bend in phase and are equally spaced). No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('spectrogram', { size: 512, seed: 7, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`.

`barchart` adds bar chart paper, bringing the current catalog from 946 to 947 kinds (948 gallery choices including plain). A pale blue-grey chart paper: two charts per tile (stacked), each with 12 dark navy bars (heights random, 15–95% of the plot area, with a slightly lighter gradient at the top), four horizontal pale-grey grid lines and a darker baseline. It is not a real chart's axis ticks, numeric labels, legend, title or multi-series data.

This material is an authored schematic of the general look of a bar chart. No specific source document, photograph or measurement is cited and no photograph was compared; the chart and bar counts (2 charts × 12 bars), bar width, height range, grid line count and width, plot-area bounds, navy and paper tones, roughness and the 0.25 m nominal tile are authored choices and do not claim to match any real chart.

A dedicated sampler draws each bar as a smooth box — a width term `smooth(clamp((0.34 − |dx|)/0.03))` plus one top term and one baseline term, each `smooth(clamp(…/0.03))` — kept entirely inside its own column (half-width 0.34 < 0.5); the grid lines are `exp(−sin²(π·steps)/w²)` inside the plot area (C-infinity, limited by a plot-area mask) and the baseline is `exp(−d²/w²)`; bar heights come from a per-column hash; everything is a convex mix; the cache totals 24 + 16,384 = 16,408 Float64 values / 131,264 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Color is pigment, bar and baseline height is about 0.6 relief plus 0.4 relief of paper grain and roughness drops 0.08 on bars; metallic is 0, there is no mortar and AO is 1. Defaults are a 0.25 m nominal tile and 0.0012 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). Measured (tool-run) at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 512² grid: bars (color<0.3) cover 25.1–29.4% and paper (color>0.85) 65.0–69.4%, color is 0.025–0.970 with a mean of 0.695–0.730, roughness is 0.54–0.62 and height is at most 0.994–0.999 relief; scanning down each column centre finds 24 bars whose heights are 13–91% of the plot area and differ by more than 0.5; the mean bar-height difference between seeds 0 and 1 is about 0.22; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (182, 189, 206), r<110 covers 26.6% and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.061. I viewed the preview: neat dark navy bars and pale grey grid lines that read as chart paper, but with no ticks or text. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`ecgpaper` adds ECG paper, bringing the current catalog from 945 to 946 kinds (947 gallery choices including plain). A pale pink medical chart paper: a 40×40-per-tile fine grid (a heavier major line every 5 cells, so 8×8 large squares), three horizontal recording strips each repeating six heartbeat waveforms (P, Q, R, S and T waves, with ±18% amplitude variation from beat to beat) drawn in a thin dark maroon line on the strip baseline. It is not a real ECG's lead labels, calibration pulse, time scale, pathological waveforms or printed text; the waveform is a simplified schematic curve (its T wave has a flat top).

This material is an authored schematic of the general look of ECG chart paper. No specific source document, photograph, medical standard or measurement is cited and no photograph was compared; the grid (40×40 per tile, major every 5), the strip and beat counts (3 strips × 6 beats), the wave positions and heights, line width, pink paper and maroon ink tones, roughness and the 0.3 m nominal tile are authored choices and do not claim to match any real ECG paper or to be usable for medical purposes.

A dedicated sampler draws the minor and major grids as one integer-count family per direction of `exp(−sin²(π·n·s)/w²)` (C-infinity, wrapping with the tile), joined by the union `1 − Π(1 − x)`; each strip's heartbeat is five compact bumps for the P, Q, R, S and T waves — `a·smooth(1 − ((x − c)/s)²)` is exactly zero for `|x − c| ≥ s` and C1, so each beat is exactly zero at its own ends and the per-beat amplitudes leave no step between beats (I first used Gaussians, whose tails are not exactly zero and left a jump of about 10⁻¹² at beat boundaries, which the C1 test magnified to about 0.038 and failed on); the trace is `exp(−d²/w²)` of width 0.0035 with `d = dy / √(1 + slope²)` the first-order distance to the curve so steep strokes keep a similar thickness, limited by two C1 windows to the vertical range the curve can reach and to its own strip; the grid and paper grain are combined and the ink is mixed in by a convex mix; the cache totals 18 + 16,384 = 16,402 Float64 values / 131,216 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Color is pigment, trace height is about 0.6 relief plus 0.4 relief of paper grain and roughness drops 0.1 on ink; metallic is 0, there is no mortar and AO is 1. Defaults are a 0.3 m nominal tile and 0.0012 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). Measured (tool-run) at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 512² grid: ink (color<0.3) covers 3.23–3.27% (3.13% at seed 7), paper (color>0.85) covers 73.8–73.9%, color is 0.05–0.955 with a mean of 0.859–0.860, roughness is 0.60–0.70 and height is at most 0.983–0.992 relief; the baseline of every strip and the top of every R wave are ink (the test verifies each beat, 3 strips × 6 beats); the ink masks of seeds 0 and 1 differ on only 0.75% of pixels (only the per-beat amplitudes and the paper grain change with the seed); in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (228, 206, 206), r<110 covers 2.9% and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.061. I viewed the preview: three repeating heartbeat traces on pink grid paper that read as ECG paper overall, though the R waves are short and the T wave is flat-topped, unlike a real waveform. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('ecgpaper', { size: 512, seed: 7, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`. Use at least size 512 so the fine grid (about 13 pixels per cell) and the trace (about 2 pixels wide) are legible.

`redalder` adds red alder, bringing the current catalog from 944 to 945 kinds (946 gallery choices including plain). It approximates an unfinished longitudinal Alnus rubra face: an even light yellowish-tan to slightly reddish ground, a fine uniform texture, two very faint darker bands, longitudinal fibre grain and very few (about 0.15%) fine dark short marks (standing in for the occasional aggregate rays). It is not a heartwood/sapwood distinction, the wide streaks of aggregate rays, knots, wavy grain or a finish.

Appearance follows the actually read [Wood Database Red Alder](https://www.wood-database.com/red-alder/) (Color/Appearance: light tan to reddish brown, darkening and reddening with age, no visible heartwood/sapwood distinction, occasional small streaks from aggregate rays; Grain/Texture: generally straight with a moderately fine, uniform texture; Endgrain: diffuse-porous with small to medium, numerous pores) and the actually downloaded and viewed [wood-face photograph](https://www.wood-database.com/wp-content/uploads/alnus-rubra.jpg) (an even light tan face, very faint lengthwise color change and scattered tiny dark short marks). These are color and grain-form references only: the wide streaks of aggregate rays, knots and wavy grain are **not** reproduced, no source image is shipped, and true color, roughness or real dimensions are not derived from the photograph; the numerous small pores are too small to show here, and a few dark marks stand in for the occasionally visible rays.

It reuses the existing Padauk/Bloodwood-family long elliptical vessel sampler by fallthrough (the same path as `blackwalnut`, `teak`, `honduranmahogany`, `shagbarkhickory`, `eastindianrosewood`, `bubinga`, `jarrah` and `merbau`); only the constructor selects the preset: a 36×12 vessel-site table (13,824 B), two undulating (bandWarp 0.8), very low-contrast (bandContrast 0.1) dark bands, a 220×9 longitudinal fibre field, 128² fine grain and the fixed 3×4 warp table, totalling 20,104 Float64 values / 160,832 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Metallic is 0; the dark marks are real height depressions while color streaks are pigment. The default 0.18 m nominal tile and 0.002 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) are authored choices. Because the shared sampler keeps the body color at about 0.25–0.46 of the palette, I chose a lighter warm-brown palette (dark (178, 124, 80) / light (246, 204, 150)) so the body color approaches the photograph's light tan. Measured (tool-run) at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 256² grid: dark marks (AO<0.9) cover 0.12–0.15%, undented body covers 99.8%, body color is 0.254–0.459, the across/along color-difference ratio is 9.98–10.64, roughness 0.50–0.602, height 0.45–0.503 relief and minimum AO 0.75; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (204, 155, 107), AO<230 covers 0.147% and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0008. I viewed the preview: an even light tan face with very faint bands and scattered fine dark marks, similar to the photograph in overall tone and evenness; the photograph is finer and more orange-yellow (my by-eye estimate is about (215, 170, 120), not a measurement). No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`sherpafleece` adds sherpa fleece, bringing the current catalog from 943 to 944 kinds (945 gallery choices including plain). A cream curly-pile fabric surface: many randomly rotated, edge-roughened cream lumps pile up into fluffy curled tufts, with occasional occluded light-brown creases between them (about 1%) and a tone and domed highlight per lump. It is not a real fleece's fibres, curl volume, woven backing or pile direction, and the preview reads more like bumpy cream crumbs or popcorn, only a loose approximation.

This material is an authored schematic of the general look of sherpa fleece. No specific source document, photograph or measurement is cited and no photograph was compared; the cell counts, probabilities, sizes and aspect ratios of the two lump layers, the edge noise, the tones, roughness and the 0.15 m nominal tile are authored choices and do not claim to match any real fabric.

It reuses the existing two-layer rotated-ellipse piece sampler of `granola` by fallthrough (the constructor only selects the preset; no new sampler): large lumps (12×12 grid, probability 1, semi-axes 0.7–1.1 cell × a 0.55–1.45 aspect) and small lumps (24×24 grid, probability 0.7, semi-axes 0.45–0.85 cell) are each jittered ±0.5 in their cell with a random rotation, and each pixel composites the pieces of its 5×5 cells in a fixed order (the lumps of this preset can extend about 1.8 cells, which a 3×3 window would cut — the reason I later widened the shared sampler to 5×5) — `value = value·(1 − m) + piece·m` with the mask `m = smooth(clamp((1 − q)/0.6))`, `q` multiplied by an edge perturbation from a 64×64 periodic noise field — large lumps first, small lumps over them, so every term is C1; the uncovered part has colour 0.3 and AO 0.4; the cache totals 1,008 + 4,032 + 4,096 + 16,384 = 25,520 Float64 values / 204,160 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Color is pigment, dome height is about 0.85 relief plus 0.15 relief of grain; metallic is 0 and there is no mortar. Defaults are a 0.15 m nominal tile and 0.012 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). I tuned this preset twice: the first version (22×22 grid, smaller lumps) looked like coarse sand or crumbs, and the second, with larger lumps, read more like fluffy tufts and was adopted; the first version's tones also let colour reach 1.01 (outside [0, 1]), and lowering the large/small lump tones to 0.52/0.58 and the dome to 0.2 brought the maximum back to 0.93. Measured (tool-run) at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 512² grid: bright tufts (color>0.7) cover 38.8–41.3%, the crease ground (AO<0.45) covers 0.92–1.72%, color is 0.234–0.931 with a mean of 0.659–0.670, the crease ground averages 0.296, roughness is always 0.92, minimum AO is 0.4 and height is at most 0.996–0.998 relief; the bright-tuft masks of seeds 0 and 1 differ on 48.2% of pixels; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (203, 191, 174), AO<200 covers 5.2% and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.788. I viewed the preview: fluffy cream lumps piled up, but not like a real fleece's fibres. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

A dedicated sampler takes the browning as `0.5 + 0.5·tanh(6·(0.5 − (0.65·broad + 0.35·fine)))` where `broad` is a 5×5 and `fine` a 22×22 periodic low-frequency noise field (the tanh makes patch edges smooth, C-infinity, and the fine noise makes them lacy); pores are `smooth(1 − q)` dimples on a 30×30 grid (about 55% chance, radius 0.14–0.28 cell, centre jittered ±0.2, so radius plus jitter stays under half a cell and each stays inside its own cell); a 128² fine grain is added; the cache totals 25 + 484 + 16,384 + 3×900 = 19,593 Float64 values / 156,744 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Color is pigment, height combines 0.4 relief of pore dents, 0.15 of browning and 0.45 of grain, and in the pores roughness rises by 0.08 and AO drops to 0.7; metallic is 0 and there is no mortar. Defaults are a 0.25 m nominal tile and 0.004 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). Measured (tool-run) at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 512² grid: browned areas (color<0.45) cover 24.7–63.4% and golden areas (color>0.6) 18.3–44.3% (they depend on the low-frequency noise, so seeds differ a lot), pores (AO<0.9) cover 4.84–5.15%, color is 0.073–0.716 with a mean of 0.428–0.544, roughness is 0.62–0.70, minimum AO is 0.7 and height is at most 0.983–0.990 relief; the browned masks of seeds 0 and 1 differ on 41.2% of pixels; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (161, 122, 73), AO<230 covers 4.87% and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.325. I viewed the preview: lace-edged browned patches and small pores on a golden ground that read as a pancake or crêpe, but patch edges show a visible blocky noise look (from the 22×22 fine field) and there is no real pancake's gloss or thickness. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('pancake', { size: 512, seed: 7, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`.

`kawung` adds kawung batik, bringing the current catalog from 937 to 938 kinds (939 gallery choices including plain). A cream wax-resist geometric pattern on dark indigo cotton: 4×4 cells with one ellipse per cell, the long axis along u in even cells and along v in odd ones (a checkerboard), each ellipse long enough to poke into its neighbours and cross their ellipses, giving the overlapping four-petal feel of the Indonesian kawung motif, with a small dot at each ellipse centre. It is not the exact geometry and proportions of a real kawung (this is a simplified schematic), the thickness variation of hand-drawn wax lines, wax cracks or dye bleed.

This material is an authored, simplified schematic of the general look of kawung batik. No specific source document, photograph or measurement is cited and no photograph or pattern book was compared; the cell count (4×4 per tile), ellipse semi-axes (0.72 / 0.30 cell), line width, dot size, indigo and wax tones, roughness and the 0.3 m nominal tile are authored choices and do not claim to match any real kawung specification.

A dedicated sampler composites the ellipses of each pixel's 3×3 cells — one ellipse per cell, its long axis along u when `col + row` is even and along v when odd (the cell count is even, so the checkerboard wraps with the tile); a ring is `smooth(clamp(1 − ((q − 1)/0.14)²))` (`q` is the ellipse form; compact and C1), the centre dot is `smooth(1 − q)`, and all join as the union `1 − Π(1 − x)`; the indigo ground also has a 5×5 periodic dye-noise field and 192² per-thread noise; the cache totals 25 + 36,864 = 36,889 Float64 values / 295,112 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Color is pigment, the wax lines are slightly raised (height 0.5 relief, thread 0.5) and roughness drops 0.06 on wax; metallic is 0, there is no mortar and AO is 1. Defaults are a 0.3 m nominal tile and 0.004 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). Measured (tool-run) at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 512² grid: wax (color>0.5) covers 12.75–12.78%, color is 0.072–0.907 with a mean of 0.2125–0.2146, the indigo ground (color<0.25) averages 0.121–0.123, roughness is 0.76–0.82 and height is at most 0.994–0.999 relief; the cell corners between four ellipses (no wax) reach at most about 0.140–0.164; the mean corner colour difference between seeds 0 and 1 is about 0.024; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (60, 64, 84), r>110 covers 13.5% and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.450. I viewed the preview: alternating ellipses and dots arranged in a pattern similar to kawung, but with simpler geometry than real batik and overly even, mechanical lines; the first version, with four petal ellipses along the grid lines, looked like a chain grid rather than kawung and was adopted only after switching to the checkerboard of ellipses. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`granola` adds granola, bringing the current catalog from 936 to 937 kinds (938 gallery choices including plain). Two layers of randomly rotated elliptical pieces lie over a honey-brown ground: larger pale-cream oat flakes (about 0.4 of the area) and smaller dark nut and dried-fruit chunks, with noise-roughened edges, overlapping neighbours, a tone and domed shading per piece, and the bare ground between them darkened by occlusion. This material is an authored schematic of the general look of granola. `merbau` adds merbau, bringing the current catalog from 929 to 930 kinds (931 gallery choices including plain). It approximates an unfinished longitudinal Intsia spp. face: a grey-tinged orange-brown ground, coarse texture, one very faint darker band, longitudinal fibre grain and densely scattered short fine dark vessel flecks (about 1.4%). It is not the vivid orange of fresh-cut wood, the yellow mineral deposits, interlocked grain or a finish.

Appearance follows the actually read [Wood Database Merbau](https://www.wood-database.com/merbau/) (Color/Appearance: orangish-brown when freshly cut, ageing to a darker reddish-brown, highly variable between boards, with small yellow mineral deposits; Grain/Texture: straight to interlocked, coarse texture, moderate luster; Endgrain: diffuse-porous with large to very large but very few pores) and the actually downloaded and viewed [wood-face photograph](https://www.wood-database.com/wp-content/uploads/merbau.jpg) (a dark grey-tinged brown face with many short lengthwise fine dark vessel marks and very few thin yellow lines). These are color and grain-form references only: yellow deposits, interlocked grain, board-to-board color variation and finish are **not** reproduced, no source image is shipped, and true color, roughness or real dimensions are not derived from the photograph; the vessel density is an authored choice following the photograph's look and does not represent the page's endgrain note that pores are very few.

It reuses the existing Padauk/Bloodwood-family long elliptical vessel sampler by fallthrough (the same path as `blackwalnut`, `teak`, `honduranmahogany`, `shagbarkhickory`, `eastindianrosewood`, `bubinga` and `jarrah`); only the constructor selects the preset: a 40×16 vessel-site table (20,480 B), one undulating (bandWarp 0.6), low-contrast (bandContrast 0.1) dark band, a 200×8 longitudinal fibre field, 128² fine grain and the fixed 3×4 warp table, totalling 20,556 Float64 values / 164,448 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Metallic is 0; the vessel pits are real height depressions while color streaks are pigment. The default 0.18 m nominal tile and 0.0025 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) are authored choices. `crosshatchengraving` adds crosshatch engraving, bringing the current catalog from 928 to 929 kinds (930 gallery choices including plain). Thin black hatch lines on cream paper are added by a low-frequency tone field: dark areas get a first diagonal family, darker areas add the opposite diagonal to form a crosshatch, and the darkest areas add horizontal lines; line width also grows with tone while highlights stay bare paper. It is not a real engraver's burin path, variable line spacing, contour lines, perspective or image content.

This material is an authored schematic of the general look of pen or copperplate crosshatching. No specific source document, photograph or measurement is cited; the line count (48 per direction), the three family thresholds (0.25 / 0.55 / 0.8), the width range, the 6×6 tone-field resolution, ink and paper tones, roughness and the 0.25 m nominal tile are authored choices and do not claim to match any real engraving or print specification.

A dedicated sampler lets a 6×6 low-frequency noise field decide the tone; three integer-count line families (`u+v` diagonal, `u−v` opposite diagonal, horizontal `v`) each fade in with a smooth ramp at their own threshold, a single line is `exp(−sin²(π·n·s)/w²)` (C-infinity, wrapping at integer counts), and the width grows from 0.06 to 0.3 with tone; the families join as the union `1 − Π(1 − x)` (not `max`, which creases where two families are equal and is not C1 — my C1 test failed on exactly that while implementing, see ACCEPTANCE), so the whole is C1; the cache totals 6² (36) plus a 128² paper grain (16,384) = 16,420 Float64 values / 131,360 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Color is pigment, ink height is about 0.7 relief plus 0.3 relief of paper grain; roughness drops 0.08 on ink; metallic is 0, there is no mortar and AO is 1. Defaults are a 0.25 m nominal tile and 0.0015 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). Measured at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 512² grid (tool-run): dark ink (color<0.5) covers 5.33–14.64% (it follows the tone field), bare paper (color>0.85) covers 70.3–87.3%, color is 0.040–0.960 with a mean of 0.796–0.883, roughness 0.72 to 0.80 and height at most 0.997 relief; the ink masks of seeds 0 and 1 differ on 8.01% of pixels; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (201, 192, 172), r<110 covers 9.6% and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.168. I viewed the four-panel render: the tonal build-up of the crosshatching is clear. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

A dedicated sampler gives each staff its own vertical pitch and each note slot its own horizontal slot, with every mark kept strictly inside its range — the five staff lines and bar lines use `smooth(1 − d²/w²)`, note heads are `smooth(1 − q)` ellipses and stems are a line profile with smooth ends, joined by the union `ink += x·(1 − ink)` — so ink reaches zero before any ownership boundary and the whole is C1; the note table is 96 Uint8 entries (0 for a rest, otherwise 1 + the pitch step) and the cache totals 96 B plus a 128² paper grain (16,384 Float64 values / 131,072 B) = 131,168 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). A dedicated sampler uses stripe = `0.5 + 0.5·tanh(5·sin(2π·4u))` (a smooth square wave, C∞, integer check count wrapping with the tile) and the same along v; color = `0.92 − 0.42·(horizontal stripe + vertical stripe)` plus the twill `cos(2π·96·(u+v))` (integer line count) and a 192² per-thread value noise (36,864 Float64 values / 294,912 B of lattice arithmetic, not total RAM); the twill and threads set height, and overlaps raise roughness slightly (0.86 → 0.90) and carry AO 0.12. I corrected two things while building: the first baseTone of 0.96 would, by my estimate (0.96 + 0.025 twill + 0.03 thread), let un-striped cloth exceed color 1 (an estimate, not measured), so I lowered it to 0.92; and the first height formula subtracted `0.1·overlap`, which made height negative at overlaps (−0.022 relief, outside [0,1]), so I changed it to `+ 0.1·(1 − overlap)`. Measured at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff: the mean of 16 points at each check center is 0.081 for double overlap, 0.502 for a single stripe and 0.921 for none; overall color is 0.026–0.973 with a mean of about 0.500; roughness is 0.86 (0.90 at overlaps), overlap AO is 0.88; the seed only changes the thread noise, so the mean sampled color difference between seeds 0 and 1 is just 0.0114; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (117, 18, 17), r<70 covers 23.6%, r>170 covers 22.6% and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.460. This material is an authored schematic of the general look of a coir (coconut fibre) doormat. No specific source document, photograph or measurement is cited; patch directions, fibre thickness, tones, roughness and the 0.3 m nominal tile are authored choices and do not claim to match any real product or material specification.

A dedicated sampler uses four value-noise lattices stretched along different directions — horizontal (12×170 cells), vertical (170×12) and two diagonals sampled with the integer shears `(u+v, v)` and `(u−v, v)` (170×12 each, which still wrap with the tile because the shears are integer) — plus a 128² fine fuzz noise and a 5×5 low-frequency patch noise; the patch noise × 4 selects the direction, the four direction weights are `cos²(π/2·distance)` (a cyclic distance, non-zero only below 1), which have zero slope at the hand-over and always sum to one, so the blend is C1. The cache totals 24,569 Float64 values / 196,552 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Color is pigment, height only feeds the normal and AO; metallic is 0 and there is no mortar. The default 0.3 m nominal tile and 0.006 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) are authored choices. At seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 256² grid: color runs from 0.007–0.053 up to 0.654–0.678 with a mean of 0.348–0.358 and a standard deviation of about 0.101, roughness is 0.935–0.965, height 0.024–0.953 relief, minimum AO 0.553–0.558 and the across/along color-difference ratio 1.03–1.23 (no global fibre direction); the mean sampled color difference between seeds 0 and 1 is 0.113; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (91, 65, 40), r<90 covers 45.2%, AO<200 covers 15.7% and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.618. I viewed the four-panel render: coarse directional patchy fibres and a strongly textured normal map. No new API or dependency; Worker/cache/texture ownership uses existing paths. This paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('coirdoormat', { size: 512, seed: 7, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`.

`europeanyew` adds European yew, bringing the current catalog from 917 to 918 kinds (919 gallery choices including plain). It approximates the heartwood of an unfinished flatsawn Taxus baccata face: an orange-brown ground, fine uniform texture, 16 dense undulating arched darker brown growth rings (about a seventh of the area) and fine longitudinal fibre grain. It is not the narrow pale yellow-tan sapwood band, a darker purplish color variation, knots, burls or a finish.

Appearance follows the actually read [Wood Database European Yew](https://www.wood-database.com/european-yew/) (Color/Appearance: sapwood usually a thin band of pale yellow or tan, heartwood orangish brown, sometimes with a darker brown or purplish hue; Grain/Texture: straight grain with a fine uniform texture and good natural luster) and the actually downloaded and viewed [wood-face photograph](https://www.wood-database.com/wp-content/uploads/taxus-baccata-300x600.jpg) (an orange-brown face with fine dense growth rings and arches and one dark knot). These are color and grain-form references only: the photograph's knot, sapwood band and purplish hue are **not** reproduced, no source image is shipped, and true color, roughness or physical size is not inferred from the photograph.

It reuses the `douglasfir` ring-index sampler by fallthrough (the same path as `longleafpine`, `westernredcedar`, `sitkaspruce`, `europeanlarch` and `europeanolive`); only the constructor selects the preset (rings 16, arch 1.9, warp 0.6, latewood 0.55–0.9, lateTone 0.32, earlyTone 0.82); a 36-value warp table plus a 200×6 fibre field and 128² fine grain total 17,620 Float64 values / 140,960 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Metallic is 0, latewood is slightly higher and ring color is pigment. The default 0.18 m nominal tile and 0.0025 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) are authored choices. At seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 256² grid: color<0.6 covers 14.9–15.2%, color>0.75 covers 70.2–70.5%, the color range is 0.469–0.881, roughness 0.421–0.490, height 0.498–0.642 relief, the across/along color-difference ratio 3.64–3.66 and the minimum AO 0.96; in the seed-7 512² maps the mean r/g/b is about (216, 143, 68), g≥140 covers 72.4% (g<140 covers 27.6%) and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0149. No new API or dependency; Worker/cache/texture ownership uses existing paths. This paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('europeanyew', { size: 512, seed: 7, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`.

`raindropripples` adds raindrop ripples, bringing the current catalog from 916 to 917 kinds (918 gallery choices including plain). On a smooth dark grey-blue water surface, 8×8 position-jittered raindrops each spread concentric ripple rings (random amplitude and phase), and neighbouring ripples superpose into interference patterns; bright and dark ring crests each cover about 6–9% of the area, the reflected color hovers around a mid grey-blue, roughness rises slightly on the waves and the normals show clear ring undulation. It is not time-evolving spreading, refraction below the surface, splashes, foam or shore reflection.

This material is an authored schematic of the general look of concentric ripples from raindrops on water. No specific source document, photograph or measurement is cited; cell count, ring wavelength, envelope radius, amplitude range, tones, roughness and the 0.4 m nominal tile are authored choices and do not claim to match any real water body or fluid-dynamics model (no dispersion, decay law or wave-speed relation).

A dedicated sampler stores four Float64 values per cell (jittered offset x, y, amplitude and ring phase), 256 Float64 values for the 8×8 cells, plus a 96² fine grain (9,216 Float64 values), 9,472 Float64 values / 75,776 B of lattice arithmetic in total (not total RAM). Ripples are summed: each drop contributes `amplitude·smooth(1 − q/R²)·cos(2π√q/λ − phase)` (envelope R = 0.78 cell with zero value and slope at the outer rim; `cos(k√q)` is even in the radius, so it is smooth at the centre too) over the 3×3 neighbour cells, and `tanh(1.1·Σ)` maps the unbounded sum to reflected bright/dark, so overlaps stay C1. Color is pigment (water reflection), height only feeds the normal; metallic is 0, there is no mortar and AO is 1. The default 0.4 m nominal tile and 0.0022 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) are authored choices. I corrected one error: the first version divided the ring frequency by the cell count again, rendering overly wide rings; after fixing it I viewed the four-panel render and confirmed fine concentric rings (wavelength 0.2 cell × 64 pixels per cell ≈ 12.8 pixels, a computed value). Measured at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 512² grid: color>0.75 covers 6.1–8.6%, color<0.25 covers 6.1–8.6% (the two differ by under 0.3 percentage points), color is 0.111–0.887 with a mean of 0.4999–0.5004, roughness is 0.080–0.122, height 0.044–0.954 relief and AO 1; along three horizontal lines the color crosses mid grey 32–66 times; the mean sampled color difference between seeds 0 and 1 is 0.189; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (115, 132, 143), r<80 covers 12.8%, r>150 covers 12.9% and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.107. No new API or dependency; Worker/cache/texture ownership uses existing paths. This paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('raindropripples', { size: 512, seed: 7, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`. Use at least size 512 so the ring wavelength (about 13 pixels) is well sampled.

`gamedice` adds game dice, bringing the current catalog from 915 to 916 kinds (917 gallery choices including plain). A tray of 6×6 ivory rounded-square dice, each with round black pips pressed into the face (the standard one-to-six layouts, rolled per die by seed), separated by a darker, rougher tray with AO; the faces are smooth and the pips recessed and rougher. It is not the three visible faces of 3D dice, tilted or stacked dice, geometry beyond the rounded rim, pip paint thickness or wear.

This material is an authored schematic based on the standard pip layouts (1–6) of a six-sided die. No specific source document, photograph or measurement is cited; die size, corner rounding, pip radius and depth, tones, roughness and the 0.3 m nominal tile are authored choices and do not claim to match any real dice specification (such as dimensions or opposite faces summing to seven), nor do they simulate how real pips are recessed.

A dedicated sampler rolls 1–6 for each of the 36 dice from `hash` by seed, with the pips taken from the standard layouts over seven candidate sites (four corners, two side centres and the centre); a die body is the product of two smooth edge ramps (flat top, zero slope at the rim) and a pip is `smooth(1 − q/r²)` pressed into the face, with tray and die colors blended by the die-body weight, so everything is C1. The cache is a 36-entry Uint8 pip table plus a 64² fine grain (4,096 Float64 values), 32,804 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Color is pigment, height only feeds the normal and AO; metallic is 0 and there is no mortar. The default 0.3 m nominal tile and 0.012 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) are authored choices. Measured at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff: the set of dark sites among the seven on every die is exactly one of the six standard layouts; across the 108 dice of the three seeds the pip counts are 21 ones, 17 twos, 19 threes, 18 fours, 21 fives and 12 sixes; face color is 0.921–0.939, pips 0.04, tray 0.16; face height is 1.0 relief, pips 0.78, tray 0; roughness is 0.30 on faces, 0.55 on pips and 0.40 on the tray; tray AO is 0.5 and face AO 1; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r is 143.7, r<60 covers 33.0%, r>180 covers 46.3%, AO<200 covers 39.2% and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.532. I viewed the four-panel render and confirmed the two-, three-, five- and six-pip layouts match standard die faces. No new API or dependency; Worker/cache/texture ownership uses existing paths. This paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('gamedice', { size: 512, seed: 7, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`. Use at least size 512 so each die is about 85 pixels.

`europeanolive` adds European olive wood, bringing the current catalog from 914 to 915 kinds (916 gallery choices including plain). It is not the deep brown to near-black streaks and veins, curly/wild grain, burl, a sapwood/heartwood boundary or a finish.

Appearance follows the actually read [Wood Database Olive](https://www.wood-database.com/olive/) (Color/Appearance: heartwood from yellow to light reddish brown with darker brown to black streaks and veins, yellowish sapwood sharply demarcated from heartwood; Grain/Texture: straight, interlocked or wild, fine uniform texture with moderate natural luster) and the actually downloaded and viewed [wood-face photograph](https://www.wood-database.com/wp-content/uploads/olea-europaea-300x600.jpg) (a pale yellow-tan face with thin dark growth lines and arches).
